comments.author: Solid-Rhoads
comments.body_html:
To your first question: the crossover quests are just an amorphous idea in my head at this point, so there’s no solid plans with regard to anything there yet.

To your second question re GZ: EFT has high level and low level ground zero now. Which one you play on depends on your level. But they’re technically two separate maps, so as a modder when you make a mission for ground zero you need to include both maps for the quest zones, sometimes this CAN cause issues when a player is actually trying to complete said quest. Again, should be fine, but just something to note.

Edit: I missed your last question (sorry, half awake lol), I’m just focused on 3.9.x for now. Not much point in speculating about subsequent versions when we don’t really have details. But odds are, if I keep up with the mod, I’m going to try to keep it current with SPT.

I’ll admit, a reference to The Maltese Falcon was not on my SPT Hub Bingo card lol. Though I do have a loose reference to ‘Double Indemnity’ in that one quest. But I have been increasingly infatuated with the idea of blending noir with semi-grounded (its Tarkov, so there’s a requisite amount of suspension of disbelief) military drama/fiction.

EFT’s designs and setting (notwithstanding the conflicting tone of some of their live action productions) have always felt a little ‘noir-adjacent western-graphic-novel’ to me. Not quite full-on Sin City, but I still look at Knight and think that could easily be a Frank Miller character. Its definitely influencing the writing to one degree or another.

But I’m spiraling into a tangent now; What I really wanted to say is, thank you. I really appreciate the feedback.

comments.author: MajorMajor
comments.body_html:
Looking at your pinned post, some more specific stuff:

  • Involving other bosses and their loot items in the narrative would open up the maps more beyond Goons. e.g.: “Leg Day: That asshole Killa keeps fucking with our power supply and making my beer warm, go break his kneecaps.” - Kill Killa with leg shots and deliver his helmet.
  • The barters are one of my favourite features, needing boss items gives them acutal value. Associated dollar cost values could be a bit higher to increase cash burn in the end game. Adding core Hideout item trades into this would make HH even more valuable.
  • Adding more alcohol deliveries to the general quest requirements would make sense with HH’s character, being a boozehound. Could even do a repeatable quest of “Deliver 6 bottles of vodka/beer/etc”. Always be scrounging for booze.
  • Don’t-do-a-thing quests would fit the narrative because ops get complicated, along the lines of “Op at the sawmill, check in at mountaintop bunker for overwatch, don’t give it away to the scavs.” - Place jammer on mountain, don’t kills any Scavs in the raid.
